https.title: HTTPS
https.intro: Certificates for every host this server answers for: from Let's Encrypt, from Cloudflare, made here, or uploaded.
https.off.title: Handled in front of this server
https.off.hint: This server uses plain HTTP, and what is in front of it, such as Caddy, nginx, Railway or a Cloudflare Tunnel, handles HTTPS. To handle HTTPS here instead, on a server of your own with ports 80 and 443, start it with:
https.off.after: Every site and management host then gets a certificate from Let's Encrypt by itself, once its DNS points here. There is nothing to sign up for. A site's page can choose another source, and HSTS works in both setups.
https.server.title: Server
https.server.listeningValue: HTTP on {httpPort}, for Let's Encrypt's checks and for redirects to HTTPS. HTTPS on {httpsPort}.
https.server.automaticValue: A shared certificate that covers the host, otherwise {source}. Names Let's Encrypt cannot issue for, such as `*.localhost` and `*.test`, get a self-signed one.
https.server.renewedValue.one: {count} day before they expire (a third of their lifetime, for shorter ones). Checked every hour.
https.server.renewedValue.other: {count} days before they expire (a third of their lifetime, for shorter ones). Checked every hour.
https.server.letsEncryptValue: Nothing to sign up for. Each host's DNS must point at this server, and the server must be reachable on port 80. Or [connect Cloudflare](dnsUrl): hosts in its zones are then checked through DNS, port 80 does not matter for them, and wildcards work.
https.server.letsEncryptValueDns: Nothing to sign up for. Hosts in Cloudflare's zones are checked through DNS. For any other host, its DNS must point at this server, and the server must be reachable on port 80.
https.server.stagingHint: Browsers do not trust staging certificates. Once they are issued, set `SiteHosting__Tls__AcmeDirectory=production` and every host gets a trusted one.
https.hosts.title: Hosts
https.hosts.unknown: That host is not one this server answers for.
https.hosts.renewAsked: Asked for a new certificate for {host}. Reload the page in a few seconds to see it.
https.shared.title: Shared certificates
https.shared.hint: One certificate for many hosts, such as a wildcard for `*.example.com`, used by every site it covers that is on automatic. Get one here, renewed by itself, or upload one; an uploaded one is not renewed, so upload the next one before it expires.
https.shared.waiting: asked for; it arrives within a minute…
https.shared.renewAsked: Asked for a new certificate. It takes up to a couple of minutes.
https.shared.removeConfirm: Remove the certificate for {names}? The sites it covers get their own instead.
https.shared.removed: Removed the shared certificate. The sites it covered get their own now.
https.shared.notFound: That shared certificate no longer exists.
https.shared.privateKey: Private key (PEM, stored encrypted and never shown again)
https.shared.saved: Saved the certificate for {names}. Sites it covers that are on automatic use it now.
https.request.title: Get a certificate
https.request.needsCloudflare: Getting one here needs Cloudflare: [connect it on the DNS page](dnsUrl).
https.request.hint: Use it for a wildcard such as `*.apps.example.com`, which covers every site under it; the bare name `apps.example.com` is included too. Let's Encrypt checks it through DNS; a Cloudflare Origin certificate lasts 15 years and is trusted by Cloudflare only.
https.request.asked: Asked for a certificate for {names}. It takes up to a couple of minutes.
https.request.error.off: HTTPS is not on in this server, so a certificate got here would not be used.
https.request.error.source: Choose Let's Encrypt or a Cloudflare Origin certificate.
https.request.error.name: {name} is not a public host name. A wildcard is `*.` and a name, such as `*.apps.example.com`.
https.request.error.noCloudflare: Connect Cloudflare on the DNS page first.
https.request.error.noZone: No Cloudflare zone the token can edit holds {name}.
https.request.error.noOrigin: The Cloudflare token is not allowed to make Origin certificates for {name}. Give it SSL and Certificates: Edit on that zone.
https.problem.noShared: No shared certificate covers this host. Upload one under HTTPS, or choose another source.
https.problem.letsEncryptPrivate: Let's Encrypt only issues for public names, and this is not one. Choose self-signed or upload one.
https.problem.originPrivate: Cloudflare only makes Origin certificates for names in your zones, and this is not one.
https.problem.notUploaded: No certificate has been uploaded for this site.
https.error.uploadFirst: Upload a certificate for this site first; uploading one chooses it.
https.upload.error.certificatePem: Paste the certificate as PEM: it starts with `-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----`. Put any intermediate certificates after it.
https.upload.error.keyPem: Paste the private key as PEM: it starts with `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` (or RSA or EC PRIVATE KEY). An encrypted key cannot be used.
https.upload.error.noCertificate: There is no certificate in it.
https.upload.error.unreadableTogether: The certificate and key could not be read together: {problem} Check that the key is the certificate's own.
https.upload.error.keyMismatch: The private key is not this certificate's own. Paste the key that was made with this certificate.
https.upload.error.unreadable: The certificate and key could not be read: {problem}
https.upload.error.noNames: The certificate names no host (it has no DNS names).
